name: Germany
summary_text: Germany is very safe for transgender visitors, with two real caveats worth knowing. First, far-right street hostility is the most documented concern: roughly 110 of 245 Christopher Street Day (Pride) events in 2025 were disrupted or attacked, over half linked to organised far-right networks — a visitor at Pride, or visibly trans in the eastern Länder, faces elevated harassment. Second, if you are arrested, prison placement follows your self-chosen civil-registry gender entry under recent state-level reforms (better than France, which still places by legal gender/ID and has subjected trans women to gynaecological "verification"), but exceptions allow placement contrary to your self-declared gender and are invoked inconsistently — a neo-Nazi provocateur who self-ID'd to female was reassigned from a women's to a men's prison in 2026 after public outcry. Offsetting this: bathrooms are unrestricted (venue-level sauna debates only), no border-police humiliation of trans travellers is documented, and carrying personal HRT through the Schengen area is uneventful. The Self-Determination Act (self-ID) is a positive climate signal though not itself a traveller-outing factor. Calibration note (Aug 2026): Germany recorded a ~35% rise in "gender diversity" hate-crime assaults in 2024 (1,152 cases) and a trans DJ filed an Equal Treatment Act complaint over degrading security screening at Frankfurt Airport — a real airport-outing incident, though resolved through a functioning legal complaint mechanism. Germany simultaneously issued trans-traveler warnings about the US and its Constitutional Court blocked an extradition to Hungary on trans-rights grounds, confirming strong institutional protections.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying France24 piece (July 2026) covers the German neo-Nazi (legally female under the Self-Determination Act) being sent to a men's prison.

sources.title: Selbstbestimmung hinter Gittern
sources.claim_summary: Verfassungsblog essay (March 2026, in German) 'Selbstbestimmung hinter Gittern' by Clara Wellhäußer: argues against a discriminatory special regime for trans people in prison following the Liebich controversy and the Self-Determination Act - constitutional analysis of trans incarceration.

sources.title: How German prisons deal with trans inmates
sources.claim_summary: DW (Aug 2023): how German prisons deal with trans inmates - climate activist Penelope Frank (legal sex 'male', identifies as a woman) faced being sent to a men's prison; the prison staff union says men's prisons are inadequately prepared and understaffed to protect trans prisoners; highlights the structural problem of binary-biological placement.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on Germany: record 84,172 politically motivated crimes (mostly far-right), with 1,765 offences targeting sexual orientation (+17.75%) and 1,152 targeting gender identity; the new Merz coalition moved to end humanitarian admission programmes including for LGBTI Afghans; Education Minister banned gender-inclusive language in her ministry (contrary to anti-discrimination advice); proposal to classify Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia as 'safe countries of origin' despite imprisonment and torture of LGBTI people there.

sources.title: German controversy surrounds jail term for transgender far-right extremist
sources.claim_summary: BBC (Aug 2025): controversy over far-right extremist Marla-Svenja Liebich, who changed legal gender to female under Germany's new Self-Determination Act (simple registry declaration) after a conviction for neo-Nazi incitement; media questioned whether the change was 'serious'; the case fuelled debate over the self-ID law.

sources.title: Germany: Gender switch neo-Nazi sent to men's prison
sources.claim_summary: DW (July 2026): Liebich, legally registered as a woman, was transferred to a men's prison after extradition from the Czech Republic - authorities cited the safety of prisoners at the women's facility; critics called the gender change a provocation and abuse of the self-determination law.

sources.title: BASHKKA files legal complaint against Frankfurt Airport for discrimination · News ⟋ RA
sources.claim_summary: Resident Advisor (June 2025): trans DJ BASHKKA filed a legal complaint against Frankfurt Airport under Germany's Equal Treatment Act after a male security officer questioned her gender during screening, refused her request for a female officer for a pat-down ('I don't care what you identify as. You're not a woman'), and laughed with colleagues - a documented airport-screening discrimination incident.

STOP the HATE (German campaign): information platform on hate crime against LGBTIQ* people - definitions, reporting, evidence preservation, support services, and cooperation with police and civil-society organisations.

sources.title: Wer darf in die Frauen-Sauna? Leitfaden sorgt für Aufregung
sources.claim_summary: RTL (in German): controversy over a guidance document on who may enter women's saunas under the Self-Determination Act - media debate about trans women in gendered facilities.

sources.title: Saunen und das Selbstbestimmungsgesetz: Wie gehen Berliner Einrichtungen jetzt mit trans Frauen um?
sources.claim_summary: Tagesspiegel Queerspiegel (in German): how Berlin saunas and similar facilities are handling trans women under the Self-Determination Act - facility-by-facility practices and legal uncertainty.

sources.title: Transgender people in prison - KFN
sources.claim_summary: Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony (KFN) research project 'Transgender people in prison': the German penal system relies on binary-biological separation; accommodation per gender identity occurs only exceptionally; the project studies the tension between the constitutional right to gender identity and presumed risks, noting a lack of data on numbers, experiences and needs of trans prisoners.

sources.title: trans*, inter* und nicht-binäre Personen in Haft - Berlin.de
sources.claim_summary: Berlin prison service official page (in German): information for trans, inter and non-binary persons in custody - rules and contacts across Berlin facilities.
